slot.brief: From boiling-point elevation or freezing-point depression of a weak electrolyte solution with known molality, compute the van 't Hoff factor and then the degree of dissociation.

stem: A weak electrolyte $\text{ACl}_2$ dissociates as $\text{ACl}_2\rightleftharpoons\text{A}^{2+}+2\text{Cl}^-$. A $0.25\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$ aqueous solution has $\Delta T_f=0.93\ \text{K}$. Given $K_f(\text{water})=1.86\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$, find its degree of dissociation.

verdicts.working: Van’t Hoff factor: $i=\Delta T_f/(K_f m)=0.93/(1.86\times0.25)=2$. For $\text{ACl}_2\to\text{A}^{2+}+2\text{Cl}^-$, $i=1+2\alpha$, so $\alpha=1/2$.

working:
$i=\dfrac{\Delta T_f}{K_f m}=\dfrac{0.93}{1.86(0.25)}=2$.
For $\text{ACl}_2\rightleftharpoons\text{A}^{2+}+2\text{Cl}^-$, $i=1+2\alpha$.
$\alpha=\dfrac{i-1}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Independent check: Van’t Hoff factor: $i=\Delta T_f/(K_f m)=0.93/(1.86\times0.25)=2$. For $\text{ACl}_2\to\text{A}^{2+}+2\text{Cl}^-$, $i=1+2\alpha$, so $\alpha=1/2$.
solution:
The van’t Hoff factor is $i=\dfrac{\Delta T_f}{K_fm}=\dfrac{0.93}{1.86\times0.25}=2$.
For $\mathrm{ACl_2\rightleftharpoons A^{2+}+2Cl^-}$, $i=1+2\alpha$.
$$\alpha=\frac{i-1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$$
